content_preview.title: DriveNets Extends Its Disaggregated AI Fabric With Two Tomahawk 6 Platforms Delivering 102.4 Tb/s for Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across
content_preview.summary: DriveNets unveiled two Broadcom Tomahawk 6-based AI fabric platforms, the liquid-cooled 2600SL and air-cooled 2601S, each carrying 64 ports of 1.6 Tb/s for 102.4 Tb/s of capacity.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

AI networking vendor DriveNets has expanded its AI fabric portfolio with two high-capacity platforms, the liquid-cooled 2600SL and the air-cooled 2601S, according to [SDxCentral](https://www.sdxcentral.com/news/drivenets-unveils-high-capacity-ai-fabric-platforms-to-connect-thousands-of-xpus/). Both systems are built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 chip and feature 64 ports of 1.6 Tb/s to provide a total connectivity capacity of 102.4 Tb/s, and they are set to ship during the current third ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece (656 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Clear Overview / What We Know / The Silicon Underneath / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure, appropriate technical depth, and an honest What-We-Don't-Know section flagging the absence of pricing, named customers, and independent benchmarks.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both snapshots read from disk and verified. source-0.html.gz (SDxCentral, HTTP 200) confirms every DriveNets specific: product names 2600SL (liquid-cooled) and 2601S (air-cooled), both based on Broadcom Tomahawk 6, 64 ports of 1.6 Tb/s = 102.4 Tb/s per system, Q3 shipping window, the scale-up (inside the rack) / scale-out (cabinet-to-cabinet) / scale-across (distributed computing) framing verbatim, the 'true 100% liquid-cooled design ... to maximize power efficiency' claim, the distributed disaggregated chassis approach, the AT&T core-routing win, and the Ido Susan and Charlie Kawwas quotes verbatim. source-1.html.gz (Broadcom GlobeNewswire release, HTTP 200) confirms the silicon specifics attributed to it: 102.4 Tbps single-chip switching capacity, 1,024 100G SerDes on a single chip, scale-up cluster of 512 XPUs, 100,000+ XPUs in a two-tier scale-out network at 200 Gbps/link, designed for 1M+ XPU clusters, co-packaged optics support, 1.6Tbps port speeds (present in the release), and the Ram Velaga 'Tomahawk 6 is not just an upgrade - it's a breakthrough' quote verbatim. Per Rule 9, DriveNets product specifics are attributed to SDxCentral and Tomahawk 6 silicon specifics to the Broadcom release; attribution is correct throughout.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, names, model codes, dates, and quotes trace to the source that carries them. No hallucinated figures or quotes detected. The internal cross-link to the Arista 7060XE7 article (2026-07/05) resolves to an existing published article. 'Pluggable connectivity' is a fair paraphrase of the release's framing of co-packaged optics as an option alongside conventional optics/copper connectivity; substance is accurate and it is a subordinate detail, not correction-worthy.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Company marketing language is properly quoted and attributed rather than asserted as fact; the Analysis section stays measured and grounded in the sourced framing.
editor_notes.originality: Genuinely new topic - no prior DriveNets coverage in the archive. Distinct from the recent Arista 7060XE7 Tomahawk 6 piece (different vendor, different products), which the article appropriately cross-links as related context rather than duplicating.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality News submission. All integrity checks pass, both sources are on the allowlist and were read from disk and verified, every specific and quote is correctly attributed, and the piece is original. Approved for publication.
